title: Applications: User-Centred Design in Action
welcome_lead: Walk in the user's shoes and design products that truly fit their needs, abilities and habits.
meta_desc: Apply user-centred design and inclusive thinking to real product briefs.
final_note: You can plan user research and turn insights into course criteria.

concepts.def: Designing around the needs of real end users.
Designing for the human body's measurements.
Data on body sizes used in ergonomic design.
Design usable by the widest range of people.
Detailed description of a target user.
Small user panel giving feedback on ideas.

walkthroughs.body_html: User-centred design starts by understanding the user profile: age, ability, context of use. Designers use interviews, surveys, focus groups and observation to gather insight before sketching a single idea.

Tables of anthropometric data list percentile sizes. A door handle designed for the 5th–95th percentile grip width fits almost everyone. Ignoring this data leads to products that exclude users with smaller or larger hands.
OXO Good Grips peelers were designed for a user with arthritis. The thick rubber handle works for everyone, showing how inclusive design widens the market rather than narrowing it.
